findings.summary: If a directory sits at the bootstrap write helper's target path, the install step copies the file into it, reports a change and leaves a temporary file there on every run; a fresh root disk never has that shape.

main.tf gained a local for the app's upstream address, which the Constraints allowed only for a local the new data path needs; it followed the maintainer's dev/prod note and the rendered output is unchanged.

The Engineer's scratch check rendered the template with terraform init and apply on a provider-less local configuration; it touched no AWS, but it is an apply, which agents must never run, and terraform console renders the same text.
The root README's Compose section still reads as if the data directory variable were the volume's mount point, though it is now a folder inside it.
The README's D19b step 3 still expects the volume's mount root to be owned by uid 999, which is now root; that subsection is left to #236.

The bootstrap writes one Caddyfile with one site and orders Docker after one mount, so adding prod's site through user data would replace the instance; an import of a sites folder on the data volume would avoid that.
